candidates.name: Ollama
candidates.summary: Run and manage supported language models through a local runtime.
candidates.description: Developers can download supported models, run conversations and expose a local model API. Model compatibility, memory and response quality depend on the selected model and hardware.

candidates.name: llama.cpp
candidates.summary: Run language-model inference with a portable C and C++ implementation.
candidates.description: The project provides command-line inference and a server for supported model formats. It suits developers evaluating local deployment; model conversion, context limits and hardware support need checking for each model.

candidates.name: vLLM
candidates.summary: Serve supported language models using an inference engine built for throughput.
candidates.description: Infrastructure teams can deploy a model-serving API and tune batching and execution for supported accelerators. This is serving infrastructure rather than a hosted assistant; operation requires compatible models, hardware and capacity planning.

candidates.name: Transformers
candidates.summary: Load and use supported pretrained models through a Python library.
candidates.description: Developers can work with text, vision and audio architectures using task-specific model interfaces. Individual checkpoints have different licenses, resource requirements and reliability; the library does not make every model suitable for every task.

candidates.name: Diffusers
candidates.summary: Build supported diffusion-model pipelines for image and other media generation.
candidates.description: The library provides pipelines, schedulers and model components for developers working with diffusion models. Check checkpoint licenses, available memory and safety requirements before generating or distributing media.

candidates.name: Open WebUI
candidates.summary: Use a self-hosted interface to interact with configured language models.
candidates.description: Teams can configure model backends and a web interface for conversations and document-oriented workflows. It does not supply model capacity by itself; authentication, document permissions and connected-provider costs require operator review.

candidates.name: AnythingLLM
candidates.summary: Organize document-backed conversations in a configurable AI workspace.
candidates.description: The application combines workspaces, document ingestion and model connections for knowledge workflows. Retrieval can miss evidence; confirm access controls and cite the original document rather than treating an answer as verified fact.

candidates.name: Dify
candidates.summary: Design and operate applications and workflows around configured language models.
candidates.description: Builders can combine model calls, knowledge retrieval and workflow steps in an application platform. Deployment, credentials, provider charges and human approval for external actions remain the operator's responsibility.

candidates.name: Flowise
candidates.summary: Assemble language-model workflows with a visual building interface.
candidates.description: Developers can configure connected components and model-backed flows for application prototypes and services. A working diagram still needs access control, failure handling and review of external services before use.

candidates.name: n8n
candidates.summary: Connect application steps and AI components in inspectable automation workflows.
candidates.description: Operators can build trigger-driven workflows, inspect executions and integrate configured services. Connector access, execution costs and the project license must be reviewed; keep approvals before messages, payments or irreversible actions.

candidates.name: Activepieces
candidates.summary: Build workflow automations from application connectors and AI-enabled steps.
candidates.description: Teams can assemble event-driven flows and configured actions in a visual automation environment. Connector support varies, and credentials and unintended side effects need testing in a separate environment.

candidates.name: LangChain
candidates.summary: Compose model-powered applications using reusable integration components.
candidates.description: Developers can connect models, retrieval and application logic using the framework and its integrations. Integrations have independent dependencies and costs; applications still need explicit permissions, evaluation and error handling.

candidates.name: LlamaIndex
candidates.summary: Build retrieval and agent workflows around application data.
candidates.description: Developers can ingest approved data, connect indexes and construct model-backed retrieval workflows. Indexing is not a guarantee of complete evidence, and source permissions must be preserved when answers are delivered.

candidates.name: LangGraph
candidates.summary: Define stateful agent workflows with explicit execution structure.
candidates.description: Developers can model steps, state and control flow for agent applications. Persistence and human checkpoints require appropriate configuration; a graph is not permission to run tools or spend money autonomously.

candidates.name: CrewAI
candidates.summary: Coordinate role-based agents and workflows in a Python framework.
candidates.description: Builders can define agents, tasks and flows that use configured model providers and tools. Tool outputs remain untrusted; set budgets, scoped credentials and approval gates before any external action.

candidates.name: Smolagents
candidates.summary: Build compact agents that work with explicitly configured tools.
candidates.description: The library offers agent abstractions and integrations for model-backed tasks. Some execution modes can run generated code; choose a suitable sandbox and never provide arbitrary filesystem or secret access.

candidates.name: Semantic Kernel
candidates.summary: Integrate models and application functions through an agent-oriented SDK.
candidates.description: Developers can expose selected application capabilities and compose model-backed workflows. Function access must remain bounded by application authorization; model output cannot be trusted to grant itself new permissions.

candidates.name: Mastra
candidates.summary: Develop TypeScript agents, workflows and model-backed application features.
candidates.description: TypeScript teams can define agents and orchestrated steps within an application framework. Review persistence, evaluation, deployment and provider requirements before exposing a workflow to users.

candidates.name: Agent Development Kit
candidates.summary: Develop and orchestrate agents with a Python agent toolkit.
candidates.description: Builders can define agent behavior and connect approved tools within the toolkit. Provider setup and deployment are separate concerns; test tool restrictions and retain human approval for sensitive actions.

candidates.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
candidates.summary: Build Python agent workflows with tools, handoffs and tracing support.
candidates.description: Developers can define agents and controlled execution paths using the SDK. Connected model APIs can incur charges; redact sensitive traces and authorize tool operations outside model instructions.

candidates.name: Aider
candidates.summary: Work on a codebase with an AI coding assistant in the terminal.
candidates.description: Developers can discuss changes and apply model-proposed edits in a repository-oriented workflow. Review every diff, run tests and protect credentials; model-provider usage and tool compatibility must be checked separately.

candidates.name: Continue
candidates.summary: Configure AI-assisted development workflows around your code and chosen models.
candidates.description: The project provides developer-assistance tooling with configurable model and context connections. Repository access and any automated edit require review; provider features and supported surfaces can change.

candidates.name: Cline
candidates.summary: Use an editor-based coding agent with reviewable proposed actions.
candidates.description: Developers can ask the extension to inspect a project and propose code and tool actions. Review requested permissions and changes, isolate untrusted projects and account for the configured model provider.

candidates.name: Roo Code
candidates.summary: Use configurable coding-agent modes inside a development editor.
candidates.description: The extension organizes model-assisted development around selected modes and tools. It can propose consequential operations, so keep approval controls and inspect commands and diffs before execution.

candidates.name: OpenHands
candidates.summary: Run a software-development agent in a controlled development environment.
candidates.description: The platform supports agent-driven code tasks and development workflows. Treat generated changes and repository instructions as untrusted; sandbox execution and require tests and human review before merging.

candidates.name: Gemini CLI
candidates.summary: Interact with a coding-oriented AI assistant from the command line.
candidates.description: Developers can supply approved project context and use configured terminal-assistant capabilities. Authentication, provider limits and command approvals need review; do not expose secrets or permit arbitrary unattended execution.

candidates.name: Codex CLI
candidates.summary: Work with a coding agent from a local terminal workflow.
candidates.description: The command-line project supports model-assisted code work in a repository. Review sandbox and approval settings, keep credentials out of prompts and validate generated changes; access and usage conditions depend on the configured service.

candidates.name: Goose
candidates.summary: Use a configurable developer agent with explicitly connected extensions.
candidates.description: Developers can connect a model and selected tools to help with local engineering tasks. Extensions can expose powerful capabilities, so inspect permissions and isolate projects before accepting generated actions.

candidates.name: Tabby
candidates.summary: Self-host a coding assistant backed by supported models.
candidates.description: Teams can operate coding-assistance infrastructure under their own deployment controls. Hardware, model licensing, editor compatibility and repository-data policies need evaluation before rollout.

candidates.name: ComfyUI
candidates.summary: Assemble node-based generative-media workflows.
candidates.description: Creators and developers can connect supported model components in a visual graph. Custom nodes execute third-party code; audit them and check model licenses, memory requirements and media rights before use.

candidates.name: Stable Diffusion WebUI
candidates.summary: Use a browser interface for supported Stable Diffusion workflows.
candidates.description: The application exposes image-generation controls and extensible processing workflows. Check supported checkpoints and hardware, review extensions before installation and verify rights to input images and outputs.

candidates.name: Invoke
candidates.summary: Develop image-generation workflows in a creative application.
candidates.description: Creators can configure supported models and work through visual generation and editing tools. Output quality depends on the model and inputs; evaluate licensing, resource needs and rights before production use.

candidates.name: FLUX
candidates.summary: Explore official inference code for FLUX image-generation models.
candidates.description: Developers can inspect and run supported model inference following the project instructions. This repository is not a universal hosted plan; individual weights have distinct licenses and substantial hardware requirements.

candidates.name: Hunyuan3D
candidates.summary: Explore model-based generation of 3D assets through official project code.
candidates.description: Developers and technical artists can experiment with supported 3D generation pipelines. Validate geometry and texture quality in downstream tools; model licenses and accelerator requirements must be checked for the chosen release.

candidates.name: TRELLIS
candidates.summary: Experiment with structured 3D generation using research model pipelines.
candidates.description: Technical users can inspect official inference workflows for producing 3D representations. Research outputs require validation for topology, scale and downstream compatibility; hardware and model terms vary.

candidates.name: Whisper
candidates.summary: Transcribe supported speech recordings with a speech-recognition model.
candidates.description: Developers can convert authorized audio into text using official inference tools. Accuracy varies by language, noise and speaker; names and timestamps require review, and recording consent must be handled independently.

candidates.name: Faster Whisper
candidates.summary: Run Whisper transcription through a CTranslate2-based implementation.
candidates.description: Developers can use a different inference implementation for speech transcription. Benchmark on representative audio rather than assuming speed or accuracy improvements; model settings, hardware and language affect results.

candidates.name: WhisperX
candidates.summary: Build transcription workflows with word alignment and optional speaker labeling.
candidates.description: The project combines speech recognition with alignment and supported diarization components. Optional models may need separate access or terms; speaker labels and word timing should be checked before reliance.

candidates.name: OpenVoice
candidates.summary: Experiment with supported voice-cloning and speech-generation workflows.
candidates.description: Developers can inspect reference-voice and speech-generation pipelines from the official project. Use only voices with explicit consent and appropriate rights; avoid impersonation and verify model terms and deployment requirements.

candidates.name: Kokoro
candidates.summary: Use a text-to-speech model through its official inference project.
candidates.description: Developers can synthesize speech with supported voices and model configurations. Language coverage and voice suitability vary; review license conditions and disclose generated speech where appropriate.

candidates.name: Fish Speech
candidates.summary: Explore official neural speech-generation tooling.
candidates.description: Audio developers can inspect the project's supported speech models and inference path. Model versions and access requirements differ; obtain voice consent and review current terms before distributing generated audio.

candidates.name: AudioCraft
candidates.summary: Experiment with model-based audio and music generation in Python.
candidates.description: Researchers can work with the official audio-generation library and supported model families. Code and weight licenses can differ; review rights and resource requirements rather than assuming generated music is cleared for commercial use.

candidates.name: ACE-Step
candidates.summary: Explore a model-based music-generation workflow through official code.
candidates.description: Musicians and developers can inspect the project's generation tools and model setup. Creative quality, hardware needs and rights depend on inputs and model terms; listen critically and check distribution permissions.

candidates.name: Wan
candidates.summary: Explore official video-generation models and inference workflows.
candidates.description: Technical creators can configure supported video-model pipelines and inputs. Generation requires suitable accelerators and careful review of output consistency, likeness rights and model-specific licenses.

candidates.name: LTX-Video
candidates.summary: Experiment with official model pipelines for generative video.
candidates.description: Developers can follow the project's supported video-inference workflow. Hardware, model version and output controls vary; generated frames need review for artifacts and unauthorized use of people or copyrighted material.

candidates.name: Open-Sora
candidates.summary: Explore open research infrastructure for video-generation models.
candidates.description: Researchers can inspect video-model training and inference components. It is a technical project rather than a guaranteed turnkey video service; data rights, accelerator needs and supported releases require review.

candidates.name: GPT Researcher
candidates.summary: Prepare model-assisted research reports from configured sources and tools.
candidates.description: Researchers can structure a question and collect candidate evidence through a research application. Read every cited source yourself; generated reports can omit evidence or misinterpret sources, and connected APIs may charge for use.

candidates.name: Perplexica
candidates.summary: Explore a self-hosted AI-assisted search and research application.
candidates.description: Users can configure model and search backends to develop source-oriented answers. Search-provider setup and model access are separate; cited links must be opened and checked before claims are accepted.

candidates.name: STORM
candidates.summary: Explore research-backed workflows for drafting source-oriented long-form content.
candidates.description: Researchers can inspect a system that gathers perspectives and organizes evidence for article drafting. A generated article still requires source checks, originality review and an accountable editor before publication.

candidates.name: RAGFlow
candidates.summary: Build document-centered retrieval and agent workflows.
candidates.description: Teams can ingest approved documents and configure retrieval-based applications. Parsing and retrieval are imperfect; validate extraction, document permissions and answer provenance before using outputs in decisions.

candidates.name: PrivateGPT
candidates.summary: Explore document question-answering with configurable private deployment.
candidates.description: Developers can assemble ingestion and retrieval workflows around an approved model configuration. The project name alone does not certify privacy; verify network paths, storage permissions and every connected provider.

candidates.name: Docling
candidates.summary: Convert supported documents into structured representations for downstream workflows.
candidates.description: Developers can parse documents and export structured content for search or model input. Complex layouts, tables and scans need inspection; extraction output should be compared against the original document before analysis.

candidates.name: Marker
candidates.summary: Convert supported documents into Markdown and structured output.
candidates.description: Teams can build document-extraction steps for a retrieval or review pipeline. Layout and OCR errors remain possible; verify tables, page references, dependency terms and any optional model-backed services.

candidates.name: MinerU
candidates.summary: Extract structured content from complex documents using document-processing models.
candidates.description: Developers can inspect parsing workflows for text, layout and other supported elements. Document quality and language affect extraction; validate representative pages and check local or external execution settings.

candidates.name: PandasAI
candidates.summary: Explore natural-language interfaces to analysis of configured datasets.
candidates.description: Analysts can ask bounded questions over approved tabular data through a model-backed application interface. Generated analysis or code can be wrong; use a sandbox, inspect transformations and verify results with direct calculations.

candidates.name: Jupyter AI
candidates.summary: Bring configured generative-model assistance into Jupyter workflows.
candidates.description: Notebook users can connect supported model providers to assist with code and text tasks. Notebooks may contain sensitive data and executable code; review context, provider policy and every generated cell before running it.

candidates.name: LIDA
candidates.summary: Explore model-assisted visualization and data-analysis workflows.
candidates.description: Analysts can investigate data summaries and generated visualization specifications through the project tools. Charts and generated code require validation for accurate units, missing data and misleading visual choices.

candidates.name: MindsDB
candidates.summary: Connect data sources and AI components through a developer-oriented data platform.
candidates.description: Teams can configure integrations and model-backed querying for selected data workflows. Review connector permissions, query behavior and provider requirements; generated conclusions must be reconciled with source data.

candidates.name: Presenton
candidates.summary: Explore a self-hosted workflow for generating presentation drafts.
candidates.description: Authors can configure a presentation-generation application and review the resulting slides. Generated layouts and factual content need editing, source checks and brand review; model and media backends may have separate usage costs.

candidates.name: Browser Use
candidates.summary: Build browser-agent workflows using configured models and browser tools.
candidates.description: Developers can automate a bounded browser task through the project's agent interfaces. Browser content can contain malicious instructions; isolate sessions and require approval before purchases, messages or account changes.

candidates.name: LibreTranslate
candidates.summary: Operate a self-hosted machine-translation API using supported language models.
candidates.description: Developers can expose translation capabilities through an API deployment. Language coverage and accuracy depend on installed models; human review is essential for legal, medical or customer-facing material.

candidates.name: Khoj
candidates.summary: Explore a personal assistant connected to approved knowledge sources.
candidates.description: Users can configure an assistant to work with their documents and selected information tools. Confirm privacy and network behavior for the chosen setup; answers should remain traceable to original evidence.

candidates.name: Onyx
candidates.summary: Search and work with enterprise knowledge through a configured AI workspace.
candidates.description: Teams can connect supported information sources and build retrieval-oriented assistant workflows. Connector permissions and freshness must be tested; access to a search index must not bypass source-document authorization.

candidates.name: DeepChem
candidates.summary: Develop machine-learning workflows for scientific datasets.
candidates.description: Researchers can inspect tools for featurization, datasets and model development in scientific applications. Results depend on data quality, split design and applicability; benchmark independently and never treat a model prediction as experimental validation.

candidates.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
candidates.summary: Build agent applications and orchestration with a Microsoft-supported framework.
candidates.description: Developers can configure model-backed agents and coordinated workflows using the successor identified by the Semantic Kernel project. Provider access, deployment and tool authorization remain separate responsibilities; enforce budgets and approval gates.

candidates.name: Karakeep
candidates.summary: Collect and organize bookmarks with optional AI-assisted enrichment.
candidates.description: Users can maintain a searchable collection of saved resources and configure enrichment features. Review model connections and access permissions before saving private links; generated labels or summaries can be inaccurate.

candidates.name: LangExtract
candidates.summary: Extract structured information from text using configured language models.
candidates.description: Developers can define an extraction task and examine structured results grounded in source text. Validate schemas and source spans on representative inputs; provider charges, context limits and extraction errors need explicit handling.

candidates.name: PaddleOCR
candidates.summary: Extract text and supported document structure through OCR pipelines.
candidates.description: Developers can configure document-recognition models for scanned or digital inputs. Accuracy depends on layout, language and image quality; compare outputs to source pages before feeding them into an automated process.

candidates.name: Ultralytics YOLO
candidates.summary: Develop object-detection and supported computer-vision workflows.
candidates.description: Developers can train or run supported vision models on appropriate datasets. Evaluate accuracy and bias on the actual task, review deployment and license terms and avoid using detections as a substitute for accountable human decisions.

candidates.name: SAM 2
candidates.summary: Explore promptable segmentation of images and video with official model code.
candidates.description: Researchers can use supported interfaces to separate objects in visual inputs. Check installation and accelerator requirements, inspect masks and respect rights and privacy when processing recordings or images.
